answer: Thread-weighted reputation pools distribute earnings only to identities whose signal strength exceeds a calibrated entropy threshold. The mechanism, reputation divergence filtering, enforces rule: identities below threshold forfeit 3.7% of accumulated rewards weekly, paid into a shared pool. Each forged identity introduces cipher noise that dilutes the original’s signal, forcing attackers to expend computational resources to mask divergence—each false node costs 0.8 validator-hours maintaining plausible activity without collapsing the harbor against manipulation.
